description: What the story's stakeholders say, each as a cartoon figure with a speech bubble — a verbatim quote where the article has one, or one line on where they stand.

voices.description: 2 to 4 stakeholders with different things to say, most important first. Each gets one figure and one bubble.

character.description: The cartoon figure for this stakeholder, by role — never a likeness of the person. Pick the archetype that fits the role, not the name: a worker wears the hard hat, an executive the tie, a judge the gavel. Use "custom" only when no archetype fits, and draw the prop in `drawing`.

drawing.description: The figure's prop, drawn as SVG shapes, for a stakeholder no fixed archetype fits — a stethoscope, a cap, a toque. Shapes only: no words, no numbers as content, no scripts, no links. The template draws the person (face, hair, shirt); this draws only the prop that names the job. Required when character is "custom", not allowed otherwise.

name.description: Who is speaking, as the article names them.

quote.description: Their words, copied exactly from the article, without the surrounding quotation marks. Mark a cut with "...". Use this when the article quotes them; use `stance` when it does not. Exactly one of `quote` and `stance` per voice.

role.description: Optional: why their voice matters, e.g. "Transport minister".

stance.description: One line on what they want or where they stand, in the article's words as far as possible. Any number in it must appear in the article. Use this only when the article does not quote them. Exactly one of `quote` and `stance` per voice.

title: Voices
